chapter: Long Branch and the war years
title: Leo Williams: from Trummy to Bird, Dizzy and Cootie
summary: After Peters went home in August 1944, Phillips got Leo Williams, who had hung out with Bird, played first alto with Dizzy and later played with Cootie Williams.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: That was until August of '44 you had that band.

Then he left. He had to go home. His mother and them made him come home. Then I was lucky enough to get Leo Williams. He just had come back from Trummy's. He was with Trummy, too. He went with Trummy when Trummy had that band. Yeah, he could blow. He could play... See, he and Bird... Bird came around here, and he and Bird hung out together all the time. Then he quit playing tenor and started playing alto. He played first alto with Diz, when Diz had his first band. Then he came around here and hooked up on that shit.
Before that phone call, you were talking about Leo Williams and he got kind of sick.
Yeah. He went with Diz, and after he left Diz, he went with Cootie.
Yeah, he stayed with Cootie's band. He played third alto with Cootie.
